newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou displeased at leaks to press regarding proposals to impose new taxes and asks Prime Minister Costas Simitis to convene party and government bodies to discuss budget after final decisions are taken and the budget is tabled in Parliament. --Main opposition leader Miltiades Evert threatens MP Dora Bakoyianni with expulsion during yesterday's 10-hour New Democracy Central Committee meeting.
--US State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns 'regrets' his statement calling on Athens and Ankara to "decide how to divide up the islets in the Aegean".
--Oppposition leader Evert battles the internal opposition. Yesterday's meeting confirms the total breach between Evert and Bakoyianni camps.

--General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) call nationwide 24-hour strike for mid-November, saaying that workers have lost 13.7 percent in real wages over the last seven years. --The 150 residents of the border islet of Agathonissi face a 1.5 hour boat ride to Samos each time they need to make a phone
--Publisher Stavros Psyharis enthroned the governor of monastic community Mount Athos yesterday before being disappearing back into the skies by helicopter.
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou invites 28 PASOK MPs to dinner to inform them of the government's work, maintaing her 'leadership profile', following her proposals for a 'solidarity tax'.
--Sweets spiked with heroin found at a primary school in
suburban Athens. Two drug dealers caught red-handed.
--Evert, Dora lock horns in public. Evert: Madam, you must
learn some respect. Dora: What's he saying?
--Rises of 30 percent in insurance premiums on the way.
